_README: LOCAL extensions to the vendored vocab.json. vocab.json is a verbatim copy of
slavesocieties/openai and must stay that way so it can be re-synced upstream;
everything we add lives here instead.
Authority: Daniel Genkins, 2026-07-29, on the 71 unreviewed ethnicity terms in
production/luna_v3/ETHNICITY_REVIEW_QUEUE.md: 'all terms are valid and should be
added to the vocabulary'.
'Added' is implemented three different ways, because the 71 are not 71 ethnonyms:
new_terms  a genuinely distinct descriptor -> a new row, appended to all three
language lists at the SAME index (the lists are positional; letting
them go ragged silently disables canonicalize() for the whole field)
variants   a scribal or compound rendering of a descriptor already in the list
-> recognized, and canonicalizes to that existing English head. No
new ethnicity is invented and no source text is rewritten.
(neither)  case, grammatical gender, and plural are handled by general
morphology rules in vocab.py, not by enumerating surface forms.
criollos, Gangaes, Macuaes, inglesa, africana, asiática, china and
india all resolve that way.
`flagged` marks terms that were added as instructed but that look like they
belong to a different field. They are listed so the decision stays visible and
reversible, not to override it.

new_terms.note: Cienfuegos/Havana 1880s: the Chinese indentured labour cohort, recorded as 'asiático'. Distinct from Indigenous.
Recorded as 'de nación africana' when the specific ethnonym was not known or not given.
Appears alongside 'asiático' in the same registers, so kept separate rather than merged into it.
Kasanje, an Angolan polity. Kept distinct from Cacanga rather than folded into it.
Plausibly a Bambara variant, but Bamba is also a Kongo region. Kept separate; collapsing on one occurrence would assert an equivalence we cannot support.
A person who escaped enslavement. A legal/social status, not an ethnolinguistic descriptor.
Means 'caste'. The scribe naming the category rather than filling it in.
An explicit statement that the origin was not known. Semantically a null, not a value.
A religious order. Belongs in titles or occupation.
Already a PHENOTYPE value. Adding it here means the ethnicity conformance metric can no longer flag a phenotype term landing in the ethnicity field.
Observed in 701157 (Brazilian Portuguese). A West-Central African ethnonym common in Brazilian registers and absent from the Cuba-weighted source list.
Observed 16x in 701157/701179. A casta term (African-Indigenous descent) standard in Brazilian records. Arguably belongs in phenotype rather than ethnicity; flagged for Daniel.

variant_notes.Indigenous: 'indio/india/Yndio/Yndia' in these registers is the source-language surface form of a descriptor already present as Indigenous/Indígena. Evidence: 201991-0279-A-02 'Tomas Yndio natural de Yucatan'. Aliasing keeps one concept in one place; a separate row would split it. 'indio asiático' is deliberately NOT routed here, since it denotes an Asian person.
variant_notes.Carabali: Eight scribal renderings of Carabalí, 14 instances. Orthographic only.
variant_notes.Congo: 'Gongo' is a C/G scribal confusion. 'Conga (Mina)' names two affiliations; it resolves to the first.
variant_notes.Monjolo: The manuscript spelling in 701157 is 'Monjollo' with a doubled l; the term is conventionally Monjolo. Recording the variant rather than correcting the scribe.

_brazilian_watchlist: NOT added: these are common in Brazilian sacramental registers but do NOT
occur in any volume we currently hold, so adding them would be inventing
vocabulary rather than recording it. Revisit if SSDA expands into Brazilian
material -- 19 of 32 tested Brazilian ethnonyms are missing, which is noise
across two volumes and systematic across a Brazilian corpus.
